page: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is a graphics-intensive server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 22 GB of dedicated VRAM, and 900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific areas, particularly in single-core CPU tasks and encryption, where stress-ng single-core and PassMark CPU encryption tests score in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and general database operations fall within the average range. Notably, the hardware excels in machine learning workloads, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference speed for prompt processing and text generation using small and medium models, alongside strong prompt processing for large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g6.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores with an Ada Lovelace architecture GPU and local NVMe storage. This hardware profile is optimized for workloads requiring localized GPU acceleration without the overhead of multi-GPU systems. It is highly suitable for LLM inference, graphics-intensive applications, ray tracing, and cryptographic processing.
